title: Historical Ingest Replay Orchestrator and Windowed Backfill Tooling
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: build a resilient, idempotent orchestrator for replaying historical ingest events into console analytics pipelines and a windowed backfill tool that product/ops can use from the Console. The orchestrator should support incremental windowing, checkpointed watermarks, dry-run validation, schema-evolution tolerance, tenant-aware rate limiting, and cost estimates. This ticket covers backend service work: a scheduler component, a compact per-window metadata store, integration points with the existing reprocess coordinator, and observability hooks. The operator flow: 1) user picks date range and query filters in Console UI (separate frontend ticket), 2) system computes optimal windowing plan (size & parallelism) based on throughput profiles and quota, 3) backend launches idempotent replay jobs per window with lineage tags and checksum verification, 4) coordinator tracks progress and retries with backoff, 5) final verification step compares aggregated metrics and surface drift/regression alerts. Must be safe to run alongside live ingestion with controlled resource limits.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can schedule and execute a windowed backfill over 90 days for a single tenant without manual intervention
All replayed windows are idempotent (re-run produces no double-counting) and carry lineage metadata for traceability
Dry-run mode can simulate the replay and output a cost and token-estimate report identical to the actual run within 5%
Console-visible controls: start/pause/cancel with per-window progress and an estimated remaining cost
System automatically adapts window size and parallelism based on observed latency/throughput to avoid SLO violations
Schema-evolution handling: when downstream schema changes are detected, the orchestrator fails fast and produces actionable error with remediation steps
Observability: per-window metrics emitted to Datadog (processed_count, failures, avg_latency, bytes_read) and an aggregated backfill dashboard
End-to-end tests and integration tests included in CI; a manual runbook exists for large replays (>30 days)
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: scoped core deliverables with PM and Data Platform. Decided to keep UI work separate; backend will expose an admin API and a preflight estimator endpoint.

2026-02-20 - Design review: agreed on using compact per-window metadata in our internal metadata-store (lightweight protobuf records). Trade-off: extra storage vs easier checkpointing and resume semantics. Miguel to prototype metadata schema.

2026-02-24 - Spike results: 1h windows give best balance for high-throughput tenants; small tenants get 6h windows. Prototype shows idempotency requires an at-least-once write with dedupe keys in downstream write adapter. We will add a replay-checksum field to events.
2026-02-28 - PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/517 (scheduling core + metadata store). Needs review from data-platform and infra. TODO: add fault-injection tests.

2026-03-02 - Review feedback: infra asked to add circuit-breaker when cluster CPU > 70% and to emit tickets if too many retries. Data Platform requested a 'validation snapshot' step that samples outputs for drift detection.
2026-03-04 - Current blockers: need export permission for historical raw events (security team approval pending: SEC-2041). Also waiting on monitoring dashboard template from Observability (DASH-88).
